description:
pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:61-111

Public API of `CtLogList` consists of:

- `new()`
- `insert(log) -> Result<()>`
- `get(&log_id) -> Option<&CtLog>`
- `len()`, `is_empty()`
- `iter() -> impl Iterator<Item = &CtLog>`

Missing for any realistic deployment:

1. `remove(&log_id) -> Option<CtLog>` — when a log is retired or
   rejected by Chrome, the caller needs to drop it from their
   trust set. Today they have to rebuild the entire list.

2. `clear()` — for "reset all trust state, start over from a fresh
   list".

3. `extend<I: IntoIterator<Item = CtLog>>(&mut self, iter: I)` — for
   "merge multiple log list sources" (Google + Apple + custom).

4. `impl FromIterator<CtLog> for CtLogList` — constructor from
   raw vec of CtLog values, with the same SHA-256 consistency
   check.

5. `iter_mut()` — to mutate `usable_from_ms` / `retired_at_ms`
   in-place when refreshing metadata. Without it, the caller has to
   `clone`, mutate, `remove`, `insert`.

6. `contains_log_id(&log_id) -> bool` — small, but common, and
   currently has to be done via `get(..).is_some()`.

7. `impl IntoIterator for CtLogList` — `for log in list { ... }`
   ergonomics; `for log in list.iter()` is the only path today.

The contract today is "build once, query, discard". A long-running
deployment that refreshes log lists weekly has to allocate-and-drop
a fresh `CtLogList` on every refresh because the type provides no
in-place mutation.

Recommendation: add `remove`, `clear`, `extend`, `FromIterator`,
`IntoIterator`, `iter_mut`, `contains_log_id` — the standard
BTreeMap-shaped accessor set. The implementation is trivial (one-
line delegations); the contract gain is large.

Note on consistency check: `insert` verifies log_id == SHA256(key_der).
The added methods should preserve this invariant. For `iter_mut`,
the danger is the caller mutating `key_der` and breaking the
invariant. Either skip `iter_mut` and provide only field-specific
setters like `update_usable_from_ms(&log_id, new_ms)`, or document
that `iter_mut` is "unsafe-ish" and the caller is responsible for
re-validating with a `Self::check_invariants()` method.

Priority P2: defensive-forcing for the production refresh use case,
not blocking but ugly.
title: CtLogList missing remove/clear/extend/FromIterator — caller must rebuild to update
